claims.quote: a modular VLA architecture combining Cosmos-Reason, a vision-language model pre-trained for Physical AI, with a diffusion-based trajectory decoder that generates dynamically feasible trajectories in real time ... AR1 employs a modular architecture that processes multi-camera, multi-timestep observations along with egomotion history and optional textual inputs.

claims.claim: AR1 학습 파이프라인은 hybrid auto-labeling + human-in-the-loop으로 구축한 Chain of Causation(CoC) 데이터셋을 사용하며, 3단계 학습(Stage 1 Action Modality Injection[이산 궤적 토큰 + conditional flow matching action expert] → Stage 2 SFT → Stage 3 GRPO 기반 RL post-training)으로 진행된다.
claims.quote: the Chain of Causation (CoC) dataset, built through a hybrid auto-labeling and human-in-the-loop pipeline producing decision-grounded, causally linked reasoning traces aligned with driving behaviors ... Stage 3: RL-Based Post-Training. This crucial stage employs Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with a comprehensive reward signal

claims.claim: 벤치마크 성능(논문 초록 기준): trajectory-only baseline 대비 어려운 케이스 planning accuracy 최대 12% 개선, closed-loop 시뮬레이션 close encounter rate 35% 감소(본문 세부: 11% vs 17%), RL post-training으로 reasoning quality 45%(3.1→4.5)·reasoning-action consistency 37%(0.62→0.85) 향상, 0.5B→7B 파라미터 스케일링에서 일관된 성능 향상.
claims.quote: AR1 achieves up to a 12% improvement in planning accuracy on challenging cases compared to a trajectory-only baseline, with a 35% reduction in close encounter rate in closed-loop simulation. RL post-training improves reasoning quality by 45% and reasoning-action consistency by 37%. Model scaling from 0.5B to 7B parameters shows consistent improvements.

claims.claim: 10B 모델(Alpamayo-R1-10B)은 'AlpaSim public benchmark'에서 0.5B 모델 대비 at-fault close encounter rate 55% 감소(4% vs 9%), AlpaSim score 2배 이상 개선(0.72 vs 0.35)을 기록 — AlpaSim이 Alpamayo-R1 평가용 공개 벤치마크로 사용됨을 뒷받침(주의: 이 수치는 alphaXiv AI 요약 본문 수치로, 논문 원문 표와 대조 검증 권장).
claims.quote: On the AlpaSim public benchmark, the 10B parameter model showed a 55% reduction in at-fault close encounter rate (4% vs 9%) and a 2x improvement in the AlpaSim score (0.72 vs 0.35) over the 0.5B model.

claims.claim: 공개 범위·실차 검증: NVIDIA는 Alpamayo-R1-10B 모델 가중치와 추론 코드를 공개했고(arXiv 원문 초록에서 URL 확인: huggingface.co/nvidia/Alpamayo-R1-10B, github.com/NVlabs/alpamayo), 도심 실차 주행 테스트에서 NVIDIA RTX 6000 Pro Blackwell 플랫폼 기준 99ms 추론 지연의 실시간 성능을 확인했다. 라이선스 종류는 이 페이지에 미기재(확인 불가).
claims.quote: The system achieves real-time performance with 99ms inference latency on an NVIDIA RTX 6000 Pro Blackwell platform. ... NVIDIA's decision to release the Alpamayo-R1-10B model weights and inference code, alongside evaluation on public datasets, provides a substantial contribution to the research community

claims.claim: At NVIDIA's GTC Taipei at COMPUTEX 2026 keynote (blog section timestamped Sunday, May 31, 2026, 8:00 p.m. PT, i.e., June 1 Taipei time), NVIDIA introduced Alpamayo 2 Super, described as an open AV reasoning model for understanding complex driving scenes and supporting end-to-end decision-making.
claims.quote: NVIDIA introduced Alpamayo 2 Super, an open AV reasoning model built to understand complex driving scenes and support end-to-end decision-making.

claims.claim: Alpamayo 2 is paired with AlpaGym, a closed-loop reinforcement learning framework for AV policy training, and with OmniDreams, which generates photorealistic driving scenarios — indicating the ecosystem tooling shifted from AlpaSim (listed with Alpamayo 1/1.5) to AlpaGym + OmniDreams at the Alpamayo 2 announcement.
claims.quote: Alpamayo 2 is paired with AlpaGym, a closed-loop reinforcement learning framework for AV policy training, and OmniDreams, which can generate photorealistic driving scenarios

claims.claim: As of May 21, 2026 (pre-keynote Best Choice Awards section), the Alpamayo open platform consisted of Alpamayo 1.5 and Alpamayo 1 — characterized as 10-billion-parameter chain-of-thought reasoning vision language action models for AV research — plus AlpaSim (open-source end-to-end simulation framework) and NVIDIA Physical AI Open Datasets with more than 1,700 hours of driving data.
claims.quote: The Alpamayo open platform includes Alpamayo 1.5 and Alpamayo 1, 10-billion-parameter chain-of-thought reasoning vision language action models for AV research; AlpaSim, an open source, end-to-end simulation framework for high-fidelity AV development; and NVIDIA Physical AI Open Datasets, which include more than 1,700 hours of driving data across geographies and conditions.

claims.claim: NVIDIA Alpamayo won the Vehicle Technology and Smart Cockpit Category Award at the COMPUTEX 2026 Best Choice Awards, announced in the blog section timestamped Thursday, May 21, 2026, 9 a.m. PT.
claims.quote: Plus, NVIDIA Alpamayo won the Vehicle Technology and Smart Cockpit Category Award for pioneering open, reasoning-based autonomous vehicle development.

claims.claim: In a section timestamped Sunday, May 31, 2026, 10 p.m. PT, NVIDIA stated that Alpamayo open models running on DGX Station bring its AV research stack to the desktop, with closed-loop driving scenarios inside virtual environments generated by NVIDIA Cosmos world foundation models.
claims.quote: in automotive, NVIDIA Alpamayo open models with DGX Station brings NVIDIA's autonomous vehicle research stack to the desktop, with a closed-loop driving scenario inside a virtual environment generated by NVIDIA Cosmos world foundation models.

claims.claim: NVIDIA launched Alpamayo at CES 2026 (article dated January 5, 2026) as a family of open-source AI models, simulation tools, and datasets for autonomous vehicle reasoning — and TechCrunch refers to the core model as 'Alpamayo 1' (not 'Alpamayo-R1'), with no mention of Alpamayo 1.5 or Alpamayo 2 in this article.
claims.quote: At CES 2026, Nvidia launched Alpamayo, a new family of open source AI models, simulation tools, and datasets for training physical robots and vehicles that are designed to help autonomous vehicles reason through complex driving situations.

claims.claim: Alpamayo 1 is a 10 billion-parameter chain-of-thought, reasoning-based vision-language-action (VLA) model intended to let an AV handle complex edge cases (e.g., a traffic light outage at a busy intersection) without prior experience.
claims.quote: At the core of Nvidia's new family is Alpamayo 1, a 10 billion-parameter chain-of-thought, reason-based vision language action (VLA) model that allows an AV to think more like a human so it can solve complex edge cases — like how to navigate a traffic light outage at a busy intersection — without previous experience.

claims.claim: Alpamayo 1's underlying code was made available on Hugging Face at launch (per TechCrunch; the article describes the models as 'open source' but does not specify license terms).
claims.quote: Alpamayo 1's underlying code is available on Hugging Face.

claims.claim: Alongside Alpamayo 1, NVIDIA released an open driving dataset with more than 1,700 hours of driving data collected across a range of geographies and conditions, covering rare and complex real-world scenarios (TechCrunch does not name it 'Physical AI AV Dataset' or give sensor details).
claims.quote: As part of the Alpamayo rollout, Nvidia is also releasing an open dataset with more than 1,700 hours of driving data collected across a range of geographies and conditions, covering rare and complex real-world scenarios.

claims.claim: NVIDIA also launched AlpaSim at CES 2026, an open-source simulation framework for validating autonomous driving systems, available on GitHub and designed to recreate real-world driving conditions from sensors to traffic (no mention of AlpaGym in this article).
claims.quote: The company is additionally launching AlpaSim, an open source simulation framework for validating autonomous driving systems. Available on GitHub, AlpaSim is designed to recreate real-world driving conditions, from sensors to traffic, so developers can safely test systems at scale.

publishDate: not stated on page (undated solutions hub; references CES 2026 video and links to GTC Taipei/COMPUTEX 2026 news, so current as of mid-2026)

claims.claim: NVIDIA's official Alpamayo page states the open reasoning VLA model family is offered at 10B parameters as 'Alpamayo 1 Nano' and 'Alpamayo 1.5 Nano', and scales to 32B parameters as 'Alpamayo 2 Super' (note: the page does not use the names 'Alpamayo-R1' or plain 'Alpamayo 2').
claims.quote: It's available in 10 B parameters with Alpamayo 1 Nano and 1.5 Nano, and scales to 32 B with Alpamayo 2 Super.

claims.claim: Alpamayo 2 Super is a 32-billion-parameter reasoning-based vision language action (VLA) model positioned for Level 4 robotaxi development, extending the Alpamayo family of open models, simulation frameworks, and physical AI datasets.
claims.quote: Alpamayo 2 Super is a 32 billion-parameter reasoning‑based vision language action (VLA) model. It extends the NVIDIA Alpamayo family of open AI models, simulation frameworks, and physical AI datasets for safe robotaxi (Level 4) development.

claims.claim: Alpamayo is built on NVIDIA Cosmos as its backbone; its inputs are multi-camera video, navigation inputs, and driving context, and its outputs are trajectories plus Chain-of-Causation reasoning traces.
claims.quote: An open reasoning VLA model for autonomous driving, Alpamayo is built on NVIDIA Cosmos™ and processes multi-camera video, navigation inputs, and driving context to generate trajectories and Chain-of-Causation reasoning traces.

claims.claim: The Alpamayo ecosystem's training/validation pipeline comprises AlpaGym, a high-throughput closed-loop reinforcement-learning training framework used to train and post-train the Alpamayo VLA models, and AlpaSim, an open-source closed-loop AV simulation framework for validating model decisions (repos at github.com/NVlabs/alpasim and github.com/NVlabs/alpamayo-recipes).
claims.quote: NVIDIA AlpaGym is a high-throughput closed-loop RL training framework, training AV models through continuous decision and observation cycles, producing models validated against the full complexity of real-world driving. ... An open-source closed-loop AV simulation framework, AlpaSim validates model decisions against real-world consequences, accelerating safety validation without scaling physical test fleets.

claims.claim: NVIDIA claims the Physical AI Open Datasets are the largest open multi-sensor driving dataset available, containing real-world driving data with Chain-of-Causation reasoning labels collected across 25 countries (hosted at huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/PhysicalAI-Autonomous-Vehicles); separately, the page states Alpamayo won the COMPUTEX Best Choice Award and links to NVIDIA's GTC Taipei/COMPUTEX 2026 news roundup.
claims.quote: The largest open multi-sensor driving dataset available, Physical AI Open Datasets provide real-world driving data with Chain-of-Causation reasoning labels across 25 countries, purpose-built for long-tail scenario coverage.

claims.claim: NVIDIA introduced Alpamayo 2 Super at GTC Taipei (press release dated May 31, 2026) as an open 34-billion-parameter reasoning-based vision language action (VLA) model for level 4 robotaxi development. The 34B figure is verified in the raw page HTML; note the GTC Taipei livestream ASR transcript renders it as '32 billion', a discrepancy likely due to ASR error but worth cross-checking against the Hugging Face model card.
claims.quote: NVIDIA GTC Taipei — NVIDIA today introduced NVIDIA Alpamayo 2 Super, a 34-billion-parameter reasoning‑based vision language action (VLA) model that extends the NVIDIA Alpamayo family of open AI models, simulation frameworks and physical AI datasets for safe, level 4 robotaxi development.

claims.claim: Alpamayo 2 Super is built on NVIDIA Cosmos world foundation models and scales ~3x versus previous 10-billion-parameter generations, which the release explicitly names as 'NVIDIA Alpamayo 1 Nano' and 'NVIDIA Alpamayo 1.5 Nano'; it is positioned as a teacher model whose distilled compact models run on NVIDIA DRIVE AGX Thor in-vehicle.
claims.quote: As the teacher model scales from 10-billion-parameter models like NVIDIA Alpamayo 1 Nano and NVIDIA Alpamayo 1.5 Nano to 34 billion parameters with Alpamayo 2 Super, a downstream AV stack built on Alpamayo inherits higher‑quality reasoning and perception from a single open release, without requiring each manufacturer to rebuild from scratch.

claims.claim: A new capability in Alpamayo 2 Super is reasoning auto-labeling with 2D grounding, which NVIDIA claims compresses annotation cycles from months to days; the model also outputs improved chain-of-causation (CoC) traces and trajectories for long-tail scenarios.
claims.quote: Introduces reasoning auto‑labeling with 2D grounding so the 34-billion-parameter foundation model can provide high-quality reasoning labels, compressing annotation cycles from months to days and reshaping AV data pipeline economics.

claims.claim: Alongside the model, NVIDIA introduced AlpaGym, a high-throughput closed-loop reinforcement learning framework that runs AV models through continuous decision/observation cycles inside NVIDIA AlpaSim (contrasted with open-loop training); the release also mentions the NVIDIA OmniDreams generative world model for photorealistic closed-loop scenario generation and integration with the Physical AI AV Dataset.
claims.quote: Where open‑loop training evaluates models against recorded data and generates a single round of actions, AlpaGym runs models through continuous decision and observation cycles in NVIDIA AlpaSim, with every braking, steering and navigation choice affecting the environment.

claims.claim: Public release scope: Alpamayo 2 Super was NOT yet released at announcement — availability is 'expected... this summer' (2026) via GitHub (inference code) and Hugging Face (model weights); the Alpamayo family has been downloaded close to 400,000 times since launch. Notably, the press release names NO specific license, NO benchmark names or numeric performance results, NO external partner companies, and does not mention CES 2026 or a non-Super 'Alpamayo 2'.
claims.quote: Alpamayo 2 Super is expected to be available this summer on GitHub for inference code and Hugging Face for model weights. [...] Since launch, Alpamayo has been downloaded close to 400,000 times.

claims.claim: NVIDIA Alpamayo 1 is an open, 10-billion-parameter reasoning VLA (vision-language-action) model that generates both trajectory predictions and human-readable reasoning traces; the blog frames such reasoning VLAs as implicit world models operating in a semantic space.
claims.quote: Part 1: Introducing NVIDIA Alpamayo 1, an open, 10B reasoning VLA model, as well as how to use the model to both generate trajectory predictions and review the corresponding reasoning traces. ... These models can be viewed as implicit world models operating in a semantic space, allowing AVs to solve complex problems step-by-step and to generate reasoning traces that mirror human thought processes.

claims.claim: Alpamayo 1's pretrained weights are openly released on Hugging Face as nvidia/Alpamayo-R1-10B, with inference code on GitHub at NVlabs/alpamayo; an example model output is a natural-language driving decision paired with a predicted trajectory.
claims.quote: The Hugging Face repository [https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Alpamayo-R1-10B] contains pretrained model weights, which can be loaded with the corresponding code on GitHub [https://github.com/NVlabs/alpamayo]. ... an example output you may see in the notebook is 'Nudge to the left to increase clearance from the construction cones encroaching into the lane,' with the corresponding predicted trajectory and ground truth trajectory visualized below.

claims.claim: The NVIDIA Physical AI AV Dataset released with Alpamayo comprises 1,727 hours of driving from 25 countries and over 2,500 cities, split into 310,895 clips of 20 seconds each, with multi-camera and LiDAR coverage for all clips and radar coverage for 163,850 clips (gated access on Hugging Face).
claims.quote: It contains a total of 1,727 hours of driving recorded in 25 countries and over 2,500 cities... Overall, it consists of 310,895 clips that are each 20 seconds long. The sensor data includes multi-camera and LiDAR coverage for all clips, and radar coverage for 163,850 clips.

claims.claim: AlpaSim, released alongside Alpamayo 1, is an open-source end-to-end simulation tool built on a microservice architecture (Driver, Renderer, TrafficSim, Controller, Physics services assignable to different GPUs); it initially ships with roughly 900 NuRec-reconstructed 20-second scenes and computes a closed-loop DrivingScore metric.
claims.quote: Introducing NVIDIA AlpaSim, an open-source end-to-end simulation tool designed for evaluating end-to-end models ... AlpaSim is built on a microservice architecture centered around the Runtime... Individual services, such as the Driver, Renderer, TrafficSim, Controller, and Physics, run in separate processes and can be assigned to different GPUs. ... The platform also ships initially with roughly 900 reconstructed scenes, each 20 seconds long ... we compute a DrivingScore that reflects performance under realistic traffic conditions.

claims.claim: This CES-2026-timeframe post (published Jan 05, 2026, tagged 'CES26', author Marco Pavone) introduces Alpamayo as a family of models, simulation tools, and datasets, but covers only Alpamayo 1 — Alpamayo 1.5, Alpamayo 2, and Alpamayo 2 Super are not mentioned, and no license terms, training-pipeline details, or quantitative benchmark numbers are stated.
claims.quote: NVIDIA introduced Alpamayo, a family of models, simulation tools, and datasets to enable development of reasoning-based AV architectures.

claims.claim: Alpamayo 2 Super, announced at GTC Taipei (article dated June 1, 2026), is a 32-billion-parameter model that replaces the previous top-end generation, Alpamayo 1 Nano and Alpamayo 1.5 Nano, which had 10 billion parameters each.
claims.quote: Previous versions included Alpamayo 1 Nano and 1.5 Nano, each with ten billion parameters. Alpamayo 2 Super replaces that generation at the top end with 32 billion parameters.

claims.claim: A new output modality in Alpamayo 2 Super is 'meta-actions' (e.g., lane change, stop, yield) delivered to a downstream planner alongside the driving trajectory.
claims.quote: New is the output of so-called meta-actions like 'lane change,' 'stop,' or 'yield,' which the model delivers to a downstream planner alongside the trajectory.

claims.claim: Every Alpamayo 2 Super decision is accompanied by a textual reasoning chain called a 'chain of causation,' which NVIDIA positions for safety documentation and regulatory review.
claims.quote: Every decision comes with a 'chain of causation,' a textual reasoning chain that Nvidia says is designed for safety documentation and regulatory review.

claims.claim: Alongside Alpamayo 2 Super, NVIDIA is releasing AlpaGym, an open-source closed-loop reinforcement-learning-in-simulation framework, and OmniDreams, a generative model for rare traffic scenarios; the article does NOT mention AlpaSim, a Physical AI Dataset, or auto-labeling.
claims.quote: Nvidia is also releasing AlpaGym, an open-source framework for closed-loop reinforcement learning in simulation, and OmniDreams, a generative model for rare traffic scenarios.

claims.claim: As of the article (June 1, 2026), Alpamayo 2 Super code and weights were not yet public but expected on GitHub and Hugging Face in summer 2026; no specific license is named for Alpamayo (the OpenMDW-1.1 license mention applies to Cosmos 3), and no external benchmark comparisons are provided.
claims.quote: Code and weights are expected to appear on GitHub and Hugging Face this summer.

claims.claim: AlpaGym is NVIDIA's open-source, high-throughput closed-loop RL post-training framework for AV models: it connects policy training to AlpaSim closed-loop rollouts and combines AlpaSim simulator microservices, NVIDIA Physical AI Open Datasets, and the distributed NVIDIA Cosmos-RL training framework into a scalable post-training pipeline (repos: github.com/NVlabs/alpagym, NVlabs/alpasim, NVlabs/alpamayo-recipes, nvidia-cosmos/cosmos-rl).
claims.quote: AlpaGym connects policy training to AlpaSim closed-loop rollouts and provides an open source, high-throughput framework for closed-loop RL. The system combines AlpaSim simulator microservices, NVIDIA Physical AI Open Datasets, and distributed NVIDIA Cosmos-RL training framework into a scalable post-training pipeline.

claims.claim: As of this post (published 2026-06-01 UTC, modified 2026-06-22), AlpaGym officially supports the Alpamayo 1.5 model at 10B parameters, with the checkpoint publicly downloadable from Hugging Face as nvidia/Alpamayo-1.5-10B. The post never mentions Alpamayo 2 or Alpamayo 2 Super (0 occurrences in page text), and the conversion tooling lives under a 'packages/policies/alpamayo_r1/' path — evidence that Alpamayo 1.5 tooling is built on the Alpamayo-R1 codebase.
claims.quote: AlpaGym currently supports the Alpamayo 1.5 model (10B parameters), which serves as an example model here, with further detailed instructions in the NVlabs/alpagym GitHub repo for how to use your own AV model. First, download the Alpamayo 1.5 checkpoint and convert it into an AlpaGym-compatible checkpoint: ... snapshot_download('nvidia/Alpamayo-1.5-10B', ...) ... packages/policies/alpamayo_r1/scripts/convert_release_to_alpagym_checkpoint.py

claims.claim: AlpaGym's training pipeline uses AlpaSim plus Cosmos-RL as its runtime/orchestration layer with GRPO as the default RL algorithm, and ships reference reward functions (e.g., a 'progress_safety' reward shown in the launch command) tested with Alpamayo models and the Physical AI AV NuRec dataset; runs are Hydra configurations and checkpoints export to safetensors.
claims.quote: It integrates AlpaSim and Cosmos RL as its runtime and orchestration layer, GRPO as a default algorithm, and includes reference reward functions tested with Alpamayo models and the Physical AI AV NuRec dataset.

claims.claim: Concrete resource/scale figures: recommended >=40 GB VRAM GPU, ~100-150 GB free disk (including ~21 GB model weights), ~1.5 GB per NuRec scene and ~1.5 TB for the full 'public_2601' suite of the Physical AI AV NuRec dataset (huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/PhysicalAI-Autonomous-Vehicles-NuRec); training the 10B model does not fit on one GPU — the smoke-test config runs on two GPUs ('tested on 2x 50GB RTX 6000 Ada', as written) and 'A distillation script to a smaller single-GPU-compatible checkpoint is planned.'
claims.quote: Recommended: a CUDA GPU with >=40 GB VRAM and ~100-150 GB free disk space (env + container images + ~21 GB weights), plus ~1.5 GB per NuRec scene (~1.5 TB for the full public_2601 suite).

claims.claim: NVIDIA launched two open AV challenges with public leaderboards at CVPR 2026: the 'AlpaSim Closed-Loop E2E Driving Challenge' (huggingface.co/spaces/nvidia/AlpasimE2EClosedLoopChallenge2026) and the 'Physical AI AV Reasoning Challenge' (huggingface.co/spaces/nvidia/PhysicalAI-AV-OOD-Reasoning-Challenge-2026); the post is tagged 'Computex 2026' and links a related post 'Taking Alpamayo to New Heights with Driving Foundation Models and Closed-Loop Training' plus the NVIDIA GTC Taipei 2026 Keynote.
claims.quote: To evaluate your model on a public leaderboard, see the two open AV challenges NVIDIA launched at CVPR 2026: AlpaSim Closed-Loop E2E Driving Challenge Physical AI AV Reasoning Challenge
